q: On an electron micrograph a mitochondrion is 40 mm long. Its actual length is 2 µm. What is the magnification?
explanation: Magnification = image size ÷ actual size, in the same units: 40 mm = 40 000 µm, and 40 000 ÷ 2 = ×20 000. Typical mitochondria are about 0.5–1 µm wide and 1–10 µm long; chloroplasts are usually 2–10 µm long. Adding a scale bar or the magnification to your drawing is good practice.
